question: does 1/L (the reciprocal log-concavity excess) add under independent sums?
verdict: FALSE -- and uniformly so: 1/L is SUBadditive, hence this bounds the excess of a sum from below, the direction Newton already gives
note: at 4-10 summands the same test is meaningless (excess ~0.6, far from the 1/sigma^2 regime); and matching arbitrary point pairs instead of a common tilt refutes nothing
